title: Characterizing local unitary equivalence of multipartite states by local unitary Bargmann invariants
authors: Yi Shen, Lin Chen, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: Local unitary (LU) equivalent states are crucial for understanding the structure of quantum entanglement. We investigate the LU equivalence based on the LU Bargmann invariants (LUBIs). We consider for which states the LUBIs are sufficient to ensure the LU equivalence. We focus on a class of multipartite states with complete local commutativity, called CLC states. We first show that for multipartite CLC states, all the LUBIs are sufficient to ensure the local permutation equivalence, if their single-party marginals are diagonal and non-degenerate. By virtue of the fact that the CLC property remains unchanged under local operations, we verify that the LUBIs are also sufficient to ensure the LU equivalence of multipartite CLC states whose single-party marginals are non-degenerate. Furthermore, when the single-party marginals are degenerate, we propose concrete examples of two-qudit and three-qubit systems, showing that there are states which share all the LUBIs but are not LU equivalent.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates when local unitary invariants (LUBIs) are sufficient to determine if two multipartite quantum states are locally unitarily equivalent. The authors find that this equivalence holds for a specific class of states (CLC states) only if the states' single-party marginals are non-degenerate. When degeneracy occurs, the LUBIs fail to distinguish between non-equivalent states.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the local unitary (LU) equivalence of multipartite quantum states using Local Unitary Bargmann Invariants (LUBIs).
main_result: The LUBIs are sufficient to guarantee LU equivalence for multipartite Completely Locally Commutative (CLC) states only when their single-party marginals are non-degenerate; otherwise, counterexamples exist.
method: The authors use algebraic invariants (LUBIs, defined via multivariate traces) and structural properties (CLC condition) to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for state equivalence.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general $n$-partite quantum states ($ho_{A_1\cdots A_n}$), with specific attention paid to the subclass of Completely Locally Commutative (CLC) states.
key_observables: Local Unitary Bargmann Invariants (LUBIs), which are multivariate traces of the state and its single-party marginals.
important_parameters: The degeneracy status of the single-party marginals is the most critical parameter determining the validity of the LUBI criterion.
main_assumptions: The sufficiency of the LUBIs is strongly dependent on the assumption that the single-party marginals are non-degenerate; the analysis is most rigorous in the CLC state setting.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general problem of LU equivalence to focusing on CLC states. It establishes sufficiency under non-degenerate marginals (using LUBIs) and then provides concrete counterexamples (e.g., 3-qubit systems) demonstrating failure when marginals are degenerate.
why_interesting: The work provides a precise mathematical tool (LUBIs) to distinguish between physically equivalent states (LU orbit) and states that merely share certain algebraic invariants, which is fundamental for characterizing entanglement structure.
